title: WebSocket / realtime channel authorization
summary: Prove a WebSocket or Socket.IO handshake or message handler omits Origin or per-message authorization, so an unauthorized client receives or changes a protected channel. A successful handshake alone is not impact.
steps: Capture the handshake and a message flow with supplied identities (GET /socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling for an sid, or a wss:// upgrade).
Compare one variable at a time: Origin on the handshake, session/cookie, channel subscription, and per-message authorization.
Cross-origin handshake: an untrusted canary Origin accepted (no Origin check) is a lead; confirm it with a protected message.

Per-message authz: as a lower-privileged or anonymous identity, subscribe or emit to a protected channel or a fabricated resource id and check for unauthorized receipt or state change with a test-owned canary message.
Do not flood, send null/malformed crash loops, or disrupt availability (ICS). One or two bounded probes only.
On PASS: unauthorized receipt or change of a protected channel with the frame evidence. For the unauthenticated get_stream url_key IDOR specifically, use socketio_unauth_stream_idor.
KILL if the handshake succeeds but protected messages remain authorized.
pass_signals: An unauthorized client receives or changes a protected channel
The handshake accepts an untrusted Origin and a protected message then succeeds
kill_signals: The handshake succeeds but per-message authorization holds
Protected channels reject the lower-privileged identity
